assertions.name: the_whole_pn_distinction_is_the_three_letter_quark_block
assertions.source: nuc11_interleaved builds both nucleons as core(6) . quark(3) . gluon(2). The core and the gluon pair are IDENTICAL between proton and neutron; only the quark block differs -- ['0', '-0.5', '-0.5'] against ['-0.5', '-0.5', '-1'] in units of h. So three letters of eleven carry the entire asymmetry

assertions.name: the_core_is_pinned_at_one_and_the_quark_blocks_are_negative
assertions.source: the six-letter gamma-gamma core has altChar = 1.0 exactly, as altChar_eq_one requires. The quark blocks have -0.910762214553 (proton) and -1.1221068216 (neutron) -- both NEGATIVE, so neither is gamma-gamma-expressible, and they are exactly where the nucleons diverge. (The gluon pair is 0.811653754366 = 1/q^2, also not 1, but it is shared and so carries no asymmetry)

assertions.name: the_alternating_character_IS_the_sign_block_computed_independently
assertions.source: multiplying the per-letter alternating characters and taking the trace of the (1,1,1) Hoefsmit projection are different routes to the same number, and they agree to 4.569e-39: -0.73922357077647 (proton), -0.91076221455307 (neutron). Without this the letter-level computation above would be an unchecked convention

assertions.name: the_corpus_separates_the_nucleons_in_the_invariant_the_ruling_pins
assertions.source: the corpus's two nucleons differ by 0.171538643777 in alternating character (23.2052 % of the proton value). Under the ruling both would be exactly 1, so this invariant could not tell them apart at all. That is not a defect in either -- it is the tension: the corpus's p/n handle is the one thing the ruling fixes

assertions.name: under_the_ruling_the_only_remaining_handle_is_the_vertex_multiset
assertions.source: a gamma-gamma word is a product of vertices sigma_i sigma_{i+1}^-1, so its only freedom is which vertices and how many; and the Markov trace is blind to their ORDER (3840 (permutation, index-assignment) pairs of a 5-vertex word give one value -- #7295, and the crossing energy is blind the same way). So the p/n asymmetry has exactly one home under the ruling: the vertex MULTISET. Stated as an assertion so the structural claim is machine-recorded; it is an argument, not a measurement, and it holds at every n

assertions.name: the_sibling_15_pair_table_is_exhaustive_at_n_equals_four
assertions.source: with 6 PSD-feasible gamma-gamma words at n = 4 (the five of #7295 plus the empty word) there are exactly 15 unordered (neutron, proton) assignments, and |tr(n) - tr(p)| is symmetric. So the 15-pair table in qbeta_qbeta_scores_a_difference_probe.py enumerates EVERY ruling-admissible assignment at that strand count -- it is exhaustive, not a sample, which is what makes its -100 %..+79.4 % span a statement about the ruling rather than about a selection

description: Q_beta is scored on a difference of a neutron word and a proton word, so the ruling must select two words and something must separate them. The corpus separates them ENTIRELY in the three-letter quark block: the gamma-gamma core and the gluon pair are byte-identical between the nucleons. And the quark blocks carry alternating character -0.9108 (p) and -1.1221 (n), both negative, while every gamma-gamma word is pinned at exactly 1 (altChar_eq_one, sorry-free) -- so the corpus separates the nucleons precisely in the invariant the ruling fixes. Under the ruling both words have altChar = 1 and cannot be told apart by it; since the trace is also blind to vertex ORDER, the p/n asymmetry has exactly one home left, the VERTEX MULTISET. Consequence: the 15-pair table in the sibling retraction probe is exhaustive at n = 4, not a sample. Scope-(a) plus one structural observation that holds at every n.

consequence.structural: under the ruling a word's only freedom is its vertex multiset -- altChar is pinned at 1 and the trace is blind to vertex order
consequence.sibling_table_is: exhaustive at n = 4, not a sample

scope.what_is_NOT_claimed: which multiset a nucleon should be; no pair is selected here, and selecting one by residual would be selection against the target
